title: Converged cluster bootstrap — field runbook (bare metal + vSphere)
body:
Context:
This is a practical field runbook for converged cluster bootstraps that need to span mixed infrastructure: bare-metal racks (IPMI + PXE) and VMware vSphere (templates/OVAs). Target audience: SREs and on-site engineers doing first-time installs and staged upgrades for Private deployments.

Purpose / scope:
- Primary: document a repeatable, low-friction bootstrap flow for clusters that will run Redwood Private control plane or inference nodes.
- Secondary: capture Terraform module caveats, verification steps, and a conservative upgrade plan for kubelet/control plane.
- Not covered here: application deployment post-bootstrap (that lives in product/ops docs).

Assumptions:
- Network/VLAN plan pre-approved and routable between management workstation and target hosts.
- vSphere templates have BaseImage v2026-01 or later with preinstalled containerd/gvisor proxies.
- PXE/HTTP image server reachable from target BMC networks for bare-metal.
- Kubeadm-based bootstrap flow with pre-provisioned CA used for initial clusters.
- Terraform 1.5+ and provider versions pinned in modules repo.

Inventory checklist (before arrival):
- IPMI credentials spreadsheet (encrypted)
- vSphere access (service account with VM create/delete, network attach)
- USB/console cables, serial-over-LAN configured
- BMC on same management VLAN or NATed to management workstation
- Signed TLS certs or PKI access if using internal CA rotation during bootstrap

High-level flow (both infra types):
1) Prepare infra with Terraform modules: net / DNS / ip allocations / bootstrap-control plane templates
2) Provision OS images (PXE for bare-metal, clone template for vSphere)
3) Run ignition/kubeadm join steps (user-data or remote exec)
4) Wait for control-plane nodes -> validate etcd / nodes ready
5) Add worker pools, configure autoscaler and node labels

Terraform module notes (observed quirks):
- Module: terraform-modules/vsphere/compute: requires resource disk UUID stable names; template cloning broken with vSphere 7.0 U3 patch on our lab (workaround: use linked clones + power-off template). See PR #256.
- Module: terraform-modules/baremetal/pxe: bootcfg generator assumes iPXE with HTTP root; for airgapped sites swap HTTP to local mirror and set MIRROR_BASE variable.
- Module: terraform-modules/ignition: ignition configs are generated from kustomize overlays — keep secrets out of git; use sops-encrypted files mounted at apply time.
- Note: provider aws/vsphere/metal are pinned in releases.tf; do not bump mid-deploy unless testing.

Common commands / snippets:
- terraform plan: terraform -chdir=infra/prod apply -var-file=prod.tfvars
- generate ignition: make -C infra/ignition generate CLUSTER=redwood-pvt-01 > cluster.ign
- manually boot a node via ipmitool: ipmitool -I lanplus -H ${BMC} -U ${USER} -P ${PASS} chassis bootdev pxe; chassis power cycle

Bare-metal bootstrap specifics:
- PXE chain: iPXE -> kernel + initramfs -> first-stage installer -> ignition fetched via HTTPS with token TTL 5m.
- Ensure BMC and OS NICs are on correct VLAN; double-NIC servers: use management NIC for provisioning, data NICs left down until OS network configured.
- IPMI quirks: Dell iDRAC versions older than 3.30 sometimes ignore bootdev set; plan for physical access fallback.

vSphere bootstrap specifics:
- Template preparation: enable cloud-init and cloud-data source, remove SSH keys from template before snapshotting.
- Use customization spec to inject management IPs when possible to avoid manual console steps.
- If cloning fails due to storage policy mismatch, fallback to template export/import and create VM from OVF.

Validation / smoke tests (post-join):
- kubectl get nodes -> all control-plane nodes Ready
- etcd health: kubectl exec -n kube-system etcd-0 -- etcdctl endpoint health
- CA cert TTL / expiry: openssl x509 -in /etc/kubernetes/pki/ca.crt -noout -dates
- Kubelet logs: journalctl -u kubelet -n 200 | grep -i error
- Container image pull: curl -I <image_registry>/v2/ (mirror validation for airgap)

Upgrade plan (conservative, non-disruptive):
1) Bake new images in staging cluster; validate application smoke tests
2) Control plane can be upgraded with maxUnavailable=1 (one at a time) if running external etcd; if stacked etcd, perform single node at time with etcd snapshot before each upgrade
3) Upgrade kubelet on workers via daemonset that rolls out cordon-drain-recreate; target maxUnavailable=10%
4) Monitor scheduler metrics and request slowdowns; increase drain timeout for long-lived inference pods
5) Rollback: restore etcd snapshot (stored in S3/MinIO bucket) then scale down new control-plane nodes and re-register old kubelet versions (documented rollback playbook).

Rollback triggers (examples):
- Control plane > 2 nodes NotReady for > 10m
- Etcd quorum lost or >= 33% member failures
- API server 5xx rate increases > baseline by 300%

Post-deploy monitoring checks (day0/day1):
- Alert: high container restart rate on kube-system pods
- Alert: node kernel OOM events
- Trace: kube-apiserver latency P95 > 200ms
- Cost: track image pull counts and registry cache hit rates

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: IP allocation collision during terraform apply -> Mitigation: run plan and manual IP audit; enforce IPAM ownership via tag in tfvars
- Risk: airgap image mismatch -> Mitigation: pre-sync images to local registry and run validation script before bootstrap
- Risk: vSphere template drift -> Mitigation: automated nightly reconcile job that compares template hash and rebuilds if mismatch

Open questions / TODOs:
- Decide default CA rotation cadence for Private clusters (15 vs 30 days?) -> draft RFC needed
- Add a terraform preflight plugin that validates vSphere storage policies before apply (ticket created INFRA-1279)
- Improve ipmitool retry heuristics for flaky BMCs (Ravi to prototype)

Quick troubleshooting notes (common fixes):
- Node stuck Pending: check CNI pod logs and kube-proxy; common for multi-homed NICs due to missing routes
- Ignition fetch fails: ensure token not expired and HTTP headers allow client CA; check proxy chains in airgap sites

Appendix: useful links and snippets
- terraform modules repo PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/terraform-modules/pull/256
- infra Jira epic: INFRA-1234 (bootstrap automation)
- Slack thread with field photos and serial numbers: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C02DEPLOY/p1678901234567

Notes to self: this doc should become a checklist-driven runbook in the Console-runbooks repo (add triggers for preflight checks). Keep this one terse and action-oriented — move design rationale to the design doc linked above.

End of runbook (draft).
